I will keep the farm simple and steady this year. I am 75, so I do not want to spread my energy across too many crops. In Quzhou County, the land and weather fit the usual wheat and maize rotation well, and I know how to manage it without making things too complicated. So I will stay with winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. That gives me grain for sale and food, uses the season fully, and is less risky than trying something fancy. I will use improved seed because it is more reliable than old seed, but I will not make the management too heavy. I will fertilize enough to protect yield, irrigate when the crop really needs it, and keep pesticide use limited to the main disease and insect times. For wheat, I will use rotary tillage because I want a clean seedbed. After wheat harvest, I will sow maize quickly with no-tillage to save labor and catch the moisture. I am assuming I will manage 10 mu in total, and I will use the same 10 mu for the wheat-maize rotation.
